questions.stem:
Arrange the sentences to form a coherent paragraph:
P: It can also preserve food and prevent spoilage.
Q: Salt has been used by humans for thousands of years.
R: In ancient times, salt was so valuable it was used as currency.
S: Today, it is an essential ingredient in nearly every cuisine worldwide.
questions.explanation: A (QRPS) is correct. Q = general introduction (salt used for thousands of years). R = specific historical detail (ancient currency). P = another historical/practical function (preservation). S = modern conclusion. Chronological flow: introduction → ancient value → ancient function → present day.

questions.stem:
Rearrange sentences to form a logical paragraph:
P: This has led to the rise of various environmental movements worldwide.
Q: Industrial activities release large amounts of carbon dioxide into the atmosphere.
R: Climate change is one of the most pressing challenges facing humanity today.
S: As a result, global temperatures have been rising steadily over the past century.
questions.explanation: A (RQSP) is correct. Logic flow: Topic → Cause → Effect → Response. R introduces the topic. Q explains the cause (CO₂ emissions). S shows the effect ('As a result' is a linking phrase pointing back to Q). P describes the societal response ('This has led to' points back to the effect). Linking phrases like 'As a result' and 'This has led to' are key signals.

questions.stem:
Which sentence must come FIRST in the paragraph?
P: However, not all forms of exercise are suitable for everyone.
Q: Regular exercise is widely recognised as essential for maintaining good health.
R: It is advisable to consult a doctor before beginning any new exercise regimen.
S: People with chronic conditions, for example, may need modified routines.
questions.explanation: B (Q) is correct. Clue words: P starts with 'However' (contrast connector → not first); S has 'for example' (refers to a prior category); R has 'It is advisable' (implies prior context). Q is the only sentence that can open independently as a complete topic statement. Correct order: Q → P → S → R.

questions.stem:
Rearrange sentences P, Q, R, S to form a coherent paragraph:
P: Therefore, reading regularly can significantly enhance one's vocabulary and cognitive abilities.
Q: Books expose readers to a wide range of language patterns and ideas.
R: Reading is one of the most powerful habits a person can develop.
S: Studies show that avid readers tend to perform better in problem-solving tasks.
questions.explanation: A (RQSP) is correct. R = general claim (topic sentence). Q = explains how reading helps (mechanism). S = cites evidence ('Studies show'). P = logical conclusion ('Therefore' is a concluding connector — never opens a paragraph). Signal: 'Therefore' in P means P must come last.

questions.stem:
Choose the sentence that CANNOT be placed immediately after sentence Q in the following:
Q: The internet has transformed the way people communicate and access information.
P: Social media platforms allow billions of people to connect instantly across the globe.
R: However, this digital revolution has also raised serious concerns about privacy.
S: In the 18th century, letters were the primary means of long-distance communication.
questions.explanation: C (S) is correct. Q is about the modern internet era. P and R both relate to modern internet effects — they can follow Q naturally. S jumps to 18th century letters without any transition, making it the weakest immediate follow-up to Q. Para-jumble logic: chronological or thematic coherence must be maintained in adjacent sentences.

questions.stem:
Arrange the following to make a coherent paragraph:
P: Vaccines work by training the immune system to recognise and fight specific pathogens.
Q: This herd immunity protects even those who cannot be vaccinated, such as newborns.
R: Vaccination is one of the most effective tools in public health history.
S: When a large percentage of a population is vaccinated, herd immunity is achieved.
questions.explanation: A (RPSQ) is correct. R = topic sentence (vaccines are effective). P = explains how vaccines work. S = describes the population-level concept. Q = consequence — 'This herd immunity' is a reference to 'herd immunity' in S, so Q must immediately follow S. Pronoun references ('This', 'Such', 'These') are strong signals — the sentence they refer to must come just before.

questions.stem:
Which of the following, if placed between sentences (1) and (2), makes the paragraph most coherent?
(1) Many experts argue that the current education system is outdated.
(2) Students are assessed almost exclusively on memorisation rather than critical thinking.
P: They believe it was designed for an industrial economy and does not prepare students for today's challenges.
Q: Online education has grown rapidly in recent years.
R: Mathematics is an important subject in schools.
questions.explanation: A (P) is correct. Sentence (1) says system is outdated; (2) says students are assessed on memorisation. P bridges them: it specifies WHAT experts think is wrong (designed for industrial economy, no critical thinking prep), setting up (2) as evidence for this claim. Q and R are completely off-topic.

questions.stem:
The sentence that must come LAST in the paragraph:
P: The findings suggest that early intervention can prevent long-term complications.
Q: A recent study examined the effects of stress on the human immune system.
R: Participants who reported high stress levels showed a significantly reduced immune response.
S: Researchers monitored 500 volunteers over a period of two years.
questions.explanation: D (P) is correct. Order: Q (study introduced) → S (study method: 500 volunteers) → R (result: high stress = reduced immunity) → P (conclusion: 'The findings suggest'). P must come last because 'The findings' refers to what was just reported. Conclusions/implications always come last. Order: QSRP.

questions.stem:
Rearrange to form a coherent paragraph:
P: Despite these challenges, many entrepreneurs continue to pursue their ideas with passion.
Q: Starting a business is one of the most challenging yet rewarding endeavours.
R: Failures, financial strain, and uncertainty are constant companions on this journey.
S: Their persistence often leads to innovations that change entire industries.
questions.explanation: A (QRPS) is correct. Q = general claim. R = specific challenges (antecedent for 'these challenges' in P). P = response ('Despite these challenges' — reference to R). S = outcome ('Their persistence' — refers to entrepreneurs in P). Key: 'these challenges' in P can only follow R which lists the challenges.

questions.stem:
Identify the CORRECT arrangement:
P: It includes not just physical fitness but mental and emotional wellbeing as well.
Q: Most people associate health with the absence of disease.
R: The World Health Organisation defines health as a state of complete wellbeing.
S: This broader definition has reshaped how healthcare systems approach patient care.
questions.explanation: A (QRPS) is correct. Q = common (limited) view of health. R = authoritative broader definition. P = elaborates on R ('It includes' — 'it' = WHO's definition from R). S = consequence ('This broader definition' refers to R, confirmed by P). Pronoun check: 'It' in P → WHO definition in R. 'This' in S → definition in R (now established). Order QRPS is uniquely correct.
